name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,340

entries.clue: Fills cash register without moving at all (5,5)

blocks.note: to stock shelves is to fill them
a till is a cash register

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper loads up the cash drawer while standing frozen to the spot.
annotation.walkthrough: The break falls in a different place in the wordplay (STOCKS + TILL) than in the answer (STOCK STILL), which is what hides it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'stock' here is an old word for a tree stump, so the phrase means as motionless as a post.

entries.clue: Canine, say, to beep horn initially (5)

blocks.note: to toot is to beep a horn

annotation.surface: A dog is told to honk a horn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog, but here it is the pointed tooth; 'say' flags it as one example of a tooth.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the pointed eye-teeth are called canines, and 'say' marks them as one instance of the category.

entries.clue: Traffic marker covering piece of wood in German city (7)

indicatorNotes.covering: CONE goes over LOG, covering it

blocks.note: a log is a piece of wood

annotation.surface: A roadworks cone sits on top of a plank somewhere in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: The cone is split around the log rather than simply placed before it.
annotation.definitionFit: The English name for Köln, the cathedral city on the Rhine; a specific instance of the general 'German city'.

entries.clue: Boy swoons regularly (3)

annotation.surface: A lad keeps fainting on a regular basis.
annotation.walkthrough: Reading every other letter of SWOONS from the start gives S, O, N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a parent's male child is often called their boy.

entries.clue: Crazy choice crucial for sport (3,6)

blocks.note: key = crucial, as in a key moment

annotation.surface: Someone makes a wild but vital pick of which sport to play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crucial' reads as an adjective on 'choice'; it is its own piece, KEY.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the skating game with sticks and a puck, Canada's national winter pastime, is one sport among many.

entries.clue: Plant found within Orbetello, Tuscany (5)

indicatorNotes.found within: the answer sits inside the following words

annotation.surface: A botanist spots a plant growing in the Tuscan town of Orbetello.
annotation.walkthrough: The Italian place names are there only to carry the letters across the comma.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the sacred water lily of Asia is one particular plant.

entries.clue: Holiday destination — extremely rude type (6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, first and last letters, of 'rude'

blocks.note: R and E, the ends of rude
a sort is a type or kind

annotation.surface: A complaint about a holiday spot full of very rude people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'rude'; it asks for the word's two ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a town or complex built for vacationers is where holidaymakers head.

entries.clue: Ugly creature to leave with most of gaudy jewellery (6)

indicatorNotes.most of: drop the last letter of BLING

annotation.surface: A hideous monster makes off with a stash of flashy jewels.
annotation.walkthrough: Bling is slang for showy jewellery.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the small, grotesque, mischievous sprite of folklore is one kind of ugly creature.

entries.clue: Respect European encounters after backtracking (6)

indicatorNotes.after backtracking: MEETS is read from the end back to the start

annotation.surface: A European earns respect after retracing their steps to meet people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Respect' could be a verb or a noun; ESTEEM works either way.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, working as noun or verb: high regard for someone, or holding them in high regard.

entries.clue: Head of transport to embrace hoodlum (4)

annotation.surface: The transport boss is told to hug a gangster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of transport' reads as a job title; it asks for a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a violent street criminal.

entries.clue: Shooter angry with show of deference (8)

annotation.surface: A gunman seethes while bowing respectfully.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' suggests a person with a gun; here it is the weapon itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a bow mounted on a stock that fires bolts is something that shoots.

entries.clue: Nobleman on blue TV show (9)

annotation.surface: An aristocrat appears in a smutty television programme.
annotation.walkthrough: COUNTDOWN is a long-running British TV word-and-numbers quiz. 'Blue' tempts toward rude or the colour; it means low-spirited.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Channel 4 letters-and-numbers quiz with its ticking clock is one particular programme.

entries.clue: Opening gold cake (6)

blocks.note: a gate is an opening in a fence or wall
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: A golden cake is unveiled at a grand opening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening gold' reads as an adjective phrase; 'Opening' is a noun, GATE.
annotation.definitionFit: The French word for cake, used in English for a rich, cream-filled layered one.

entries.clue: Stunned by labyrinth appearing in advert (6)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: something appearing in an advert is shown within it, so the labyrinth sits inside the ad's letters

annotation.surface: A viewer is dazzled by a maze shown in a commercial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stunned by' reads naturally together, but 'by' is only the link to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe being struck speechless with astonishment.

entries.clue: King facing a judge in martial art (6)

annotation.surface: A monarch squares up to a magistrate in a fighting contest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun, a person in court; it is the verb, to rate.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Japanese unarmed fighting discipline of strikes and kicks is one martial art.

entries.clue: Subdue concerning journalism (7)

annotation.surface: A regime cracks down on reporting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a censorship headline, which neatly covers both halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to hold down or quell, whether a people or a feeling.

entries.clue: Stray pet savaged wall hanging (8)

indicatorNotes.savaged: the letters are torn apart and rearranged

annotation.surface: A stray animal rips a hanging on the wall to shreds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Savaged' reads as the animal's attack on the hanging, so the surface hides the signal in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a woven picture textile is the classic thing hung on a wall.

entries.clue: Maxes out tests (5)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters of 'maxes' are put out of order

annotation.surface: A student scores top marks on every paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maxes out' reads as a phrasal verb, to hit the limit; 'out' is really the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: short for examinations, the formal written or oral tests set in schools.

entries.clue: Drink knocked back next to a city in Italy (4)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: SIP is turned back to front

annotation.surface: A drink downed in one beside an Italian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like gulping a drink; it turns SIP around.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Tuscan home of the Leaning Tower is one city in Italy.

entries.clue: Incantation period (5)

blocks.note: a set of magic words chanted by a witch or wizard
a stretch of time, as of weather or work

annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of one word: the magic formula, and a cold spell or a spell in charge.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are plain synonyms: a wizard casts one kind, and a stretch of bad weather is the other kind.

entries.clue: Do leap off pleasure craft (6)

annotation.surface: Someone is urged to jump from a holiday boat.
annotation.walkthrough: A pedalo is a small pedal-powered boat hired at British seaside resorts. 'Off' reads as 'jump off'; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pedal-powered boat hired for fun on a lake or beach is one kind of pleasure craft.

entries.clue: Author on river to become more intense (6)

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

annotation.surface: A writer by the river feels their emotions grow stronger.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' places the writing piece after the river. 'Author' looks like a noun but works as the verb, to write.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a colour, a crisis or a friendship grows stronger or more profound.

entries.clue: Medic does operations clumsily at first (3)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

annotation.surface: A surgeon botches procedures early in their career.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' seems to be about a new doctor's early days; it picks out the opening letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A doc is an informal word for a doctor.

entries.clue: Some directors and cast leave seaside production? (10)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the following words are used

annotation.surface: Film crew and actors walk out of a production set by the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Production' sounds theatrical, fitting directors and cast; the question mark warns it is a playful definition for something built on the beach.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic stretch: 'production' means something made, and what children make on the beach is a mound of moulded sand.
